svg.title: Build a Placement-Ready Desk in Thirty Days
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Build a Placement-Ready Desk in Thirty Days; subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish evidence before expanding lease exposure.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The sprint prepares operations; canonical time to first deal remains one to three months. Numeric values are milestone end days, not expected placements. Initial commitments must fit available capital and documented payer demand.; caption: End the month with permissioned inventory, tested billing, clear responsibility, and a controlled live-placement pipeline.; stages: label: Days 1–7; value: Choose one service area and document operating constraints; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Map landlord permission requirements, occupancy taxes, habitability rules, and insurance needs. Build a thirteen-week cash forecast using the $3,000–$18,000 monthly operating-expense envelope and separately model landlord rent and utility pass-through timing.; label: Days 8–14; value: Qualify inventory and complete the property permission file; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Inspect candidate units, obtain furnishing quotes, and negotiate explicit corporate-housing sublease addenda. Obtain broker coverage confirmation and calculate the cash loss from an early departure followed by an unfilled lease period.; label: Days 15–21; value: Test intake, extension tracking, access, and invoice reconciliation; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Configure Airtable records, authorized portal exports, QuickBooks Online invoice mapping, and smart-lock expiry. Run a synthetic placement through extension, utility overage, partial payment, and early-closeout cases without transmitting invented customer records.; label: Days 22–30; value: Open qualified referrals and review every proposed commitment; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Contact relevant insurance housing coordinators and corporate relocation desks with verified inventory facts. Track the nested request cohort, evaluate signed payer terms, and commit only exposure the cash forecast can support if first collection slips.

rect.title: label: Days 1–7; value: Choose one service area and document operating constraints; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Map landlord permission requirements, occupancy taxes, habitability rules, and insurance needs. Build a thirteen-week cash forecast using the $3,000–$18,000 monthly operating-expense envelope and separately model landlord rent and utility pass-through timing.
